manuscript_title: Will the World's Population Keep Growing? A Component-Resolved, Calibrated Proposal for Population-Peak Persistence
central_hypothesis: A jointly calibrated probabilistic cohort-component ensemble can distinguish post-2100 growth-persistence conditions from earlier-peak conditions; climate-disruption covariates are retained only if they improve held-out prediction and calibration beyond demographic components alone.
mechanism: Fertility, survival, and net migration update country-age-sex cohorts. Posterior trajectories are aggregated before calculating annual global growth and first-peak year. Climate features are predictive-only ablations.
alternatives: Starting age structure and fertility convergence explain peak timing without climate features.
Climate feature value is confounding or measurement artifact.
Structural uncertainty cannot be sufficiently constrained by historical validation.
falsification_criteria: A simpler demographic baseline matches or exceeds the complex ensemble on held-out primary metrics.
The climate ablation does not improve predictive performance.
The persistence decision is unstable to input vintage, priors, or aggregation.
must_include: direction-selection audit with no fabricated MCTS history
must_not_include: observed simulations, forecasts, or model scores
a claim that population will definitely peak or grow indefinitely
new citations, evidence, or mechanisms outside the Survey registry
filler text solely to reach a page count
human_review_items: communication risk relating to reproductive autonomy and migration
